P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but notes not read back — 'know you spoke with Kim, he, uh, kind of gave me a head start on you. So I understand.' The frame is the same three-part version this rep uses on every call: 'I just want to get a good idea of where you're at, build out what it is that you want. And then if there's alignment, we can talk about the coaching. If not, that's fine as well.' Missing what's in the way and what you need. Agreement asked and given ('Alrighty.' / 'Absolutely.'). Open question asked verbatim: 'What was it that you were hoping we could potentially help you with, man?'

P2.evidence: Much the strongest baseline in the batch. Weight asked directly and pinned to history — 'how much do you weigh right now?' (198 lb), then start weight (220) and low point (~175). Age was volunteered rather than asked and height was never taken, so P2a is partial. Work was explored thoroughly: flight attendant, the sporadic roster, the second property-management job and its last day. Training now was asked ('Are you training now?') and results from it followed up ('How are you finding it?'), which produced the posture story. Diet asked with a callback to the keto history. Sleep and energy asked together and properly: 'what's your sleep like and your energy levels?', then pushed on the cause — 'your work schedule not very forgiving when it comes to this is bedtime, this is wake-up time?'. The hip was probed rather than accepted — 'with the hip, did they tell you what it is exactly?' and 'They said it was, like, minor, in a way' — though duration was never asked and hereditary conditions were never raised.

P3.evidence: The six-month question was asked cleanly and the vague answer was pushed on rather than accepted: 'When you say feel healthier, is that more in terms of, like, I guess a good word would be vitality in a way?' and 'if you were going to be super specific with what is healthy'. The deep question then produced the best moment in the corpus so far — 'when you get to the point you want to get to... what changes?' — which surfaced a genuine fear of success: 'it would almost feel bittersweet, but probably more bitter than sweet... what other thing do you have that you want to like strive towards?' The rep handled it well with the Michael Jordan ladder. But he then stayed in the psychology and never turned the corner the script asks for: no 'who else does that impact', no family, no legacy, no reflect-back, and nothing physical he wants to do and cannot. Identity was touched only through the prospect's own 'I want to feel like I'm 34, not like I'm 50'.

P4.evidence: Best past-attempts work in the batch. 'What have you tried?' asked directly at 00:03:01, producing the full keto arc, and followed through on outcome — the numbers were pinned down turn by turn ('you put like half of it back on', 'you said it was over a couple of years'). The blocker question was asked properly: 'is it the hip, the main thing that's holding you back or is there anything else that holds you back sometimes?', which produced the roster and the equipment-access problem, and the rep then solved it live by restructuring to two kettlebell days and two calisthenics days. Why it did not stick was explained by the prospect rather than asked for, and the P4f line — the information is not the problem, why can't you stick to it alone — was never run, which matters because the prospect is currently paying someone else $200 a month for exactly the information.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame anywhere in seventy-five minutes. No two-year question, no 'willing to settle', no 'why not'. The line in the sand was asked twice and answered — 'The question I would have is, do you want it?' and 'are you ready to be courageous in overcoming those to get what you want?' / 'Absolutely. Yes.' This is the decisive omission on this call. The objection that killed it was a priority objection dressed as an affordability objection, and the only thing that answers a priority objection is a cost of inaction. The rep had the raw material sitting there — waking up feeling hit by a bus, never having shifted the belly fat in 34 years, feeling fifty at 34 — and used none of it.

P6.evidence: A readiness check ran before the offer and got a clean yes — 'are you ready to be courageous in overcoming those to get what you want?' / 'Absolutely. Yes.' — so P6c is satisfied. But the belief question the script actually specifies, whether he can get there with the right structure and the right person in his corner, was only asked after the price had landed, as the isolation move: 'money aside, do you feel as though you're a hundred percent confident that you'll get where you want to go with it.' It got an emphatic yes, which is exactly why asking it earlier would have been worth so much. The all-in question — if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in — was never asked, and it is the one move that would have surfaced the finances before rather than after the number.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted ('What do you want to do, my friend?') and declined pending 24 hours, so none of the payment or onboarding steps were reachable. A Stripe link was sent but explicitly as a Klarna eligibility test rather than a purchase — 'This isn't you signing up for anything' — and it returned declined. The Trevor onboarding call was described in advance (Monday or Tuesday, tailored plans 24-48 hours later) but not booked; what was booked was a second sales call.

objection_plays.detail: The framing half ran better than anywhere else in the batch. Isolation was clean and got an unqualified yes: 'money aside, do you feel as though you're a hundred percent confident that you'll get where you want to go with it.' The should-I-versus-how frame ran almost verbatim: 'It's not a, it's not should I do this, it's how do I make it work?' The break-it-up move ran: 'we can make it work in whatever way, you don't have to do it all upfront.' The financial-picture half did not run at all — no permission question for an open financial conversation, no cash on hand, no monthly surplus after bills, no number of cards, no available credit, no used-versus-available, no investments. In their place the rep asked only for a credit score and pushed a Klarna application. The consequence is concrete: a prospect who had just quit his second job two weeks after a pay rise was steered toward a $650-a-month commitment without anyone establishing what his monthly surplus on one income actually is — a figure he himself said he did not yet know.

Trigger explicit: 'don't make the decision right here right now just like you did with the nutritional program... you need to take a step back.' The rep ran the can-it-get-you-there move (already answered yes), and ran a strong version of what's-actually-coming-up by calling back to the two fears he had pre-framed at 00:29:00 — an unusually good piece of setup. He also ran a variant of the deciding-not-thinking move as 'In that time, are you going to look for reasons why you should do it or reasons why you shouldn't do it?'. Not run: 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is' in substance, the when-do-you-make-a-different-decision move, the man-you-want-to-be move, and the final are-you-sure sweep. He ultimately conceded the 24 hours, which was arguably correct here given the prospect's stated reason was arithmetic he genuinely had not done yet.

Triggered repeatedly — 'I want it, and I'm scared', 'I'm nervous, man', 'that number is scary. And that number is really scary.' The burned-before move ran textbook and was the strongest single piece of objection handling in the batch: he pre-empted it before the price ('the other thing is that you just spent money on a nutritionist and you don't feel like you've got the results you want... It's like the first time you fall off your bike') and then closed the loop after it ('you didn't make a bad decision two months ago with the nutrition thing. In fact, you made a good decision because you made the decision to change'). The plane image was replaced with skydiving, which is a fair substitute. The how-will-you-know-if-you-never-try move ran as 'If you knew you couldn't fail, would you do it?'. Not run: the certainty question, and the toward-pleasure-or-away-from-pain question.

Clinical fit. The prospect has a hip injury under active physical therapy assigned by his primary doctor. The rep did more here than on any other call in the batch — he asked what the diagnosis was, established that no imaging or surgery was indicated, and registered that it was assessed as minor. That is closer to a clearance conversation than anything else in this rep's calls. What is still missing, because the script contains nothing to prompt it, is the actual question: has the treating physiotherapist cleared loaded ballistic kettlebell work, and does this programme run alongside or instead of the physical therapy? Instead the programme was positioned as the thing that would fix it — 'let us know about the hips, right? We need to see how you move so we can fix that. Cause we don't want you feeling that way anymore.'

notes: The best-run call in the batch on discovery and the worst outcome on price discipline. Baseline and past-attempts were genuinely strong, the fear-of-success question got somewhere real, and both objections were pre-framed twenty minutes before they arrived. Then two things went wrong. First, no consequence frame was ever built, so when the number landed there was no cost of inaction to weigh it against and the conversation became a debate about interpretation. Second, having skipped the entire financial-picture half of OC, the rep filled the gap with financing — a Klarna application and a $650-a-month plan — for a man who had said in plain terms that he did not yet know what his income would be. Coach this rep on P5 and on asking for actual numbers before offering payment structures; his rapport and his discovery are already ahead of the rest of the batch.
